# Multi-label activity head — results

*Auto-generated by `ml/scripts/eval_esm_multiclass.py`. Bootstrap n=1000, seed=42.*

Architecture: same 3-layer MLP head as the binary Phase 2B model, but with 4 sigmoid outputs (multi-label). Trained on the AMP-positive subset of the cluster-aware splits, using ESM2-650M frozen embeddings as input.

Checkpoint: epoch 11, val macro-AUC 0.8050.

## Per-class test AUC (n=882 AMP positives in held-out test)

| activity | n_pos | n_neg | AUC (95% CI) |
|---|---|---|---|
| antibacterial | 854 | 28 | 0.809 [0.746-0.864] |
| antifungal | 66 | 816 | 0.730 [0.668-0.787] |
| antiviral | 218 | 664 | 0.872 [0.844-0.898] |
| antiparasitic | 5 | 877 | 0.811 [0.547-0.979] |

**Macro-AUC** (mean over classes with sufficient test positives): **0.8055**

## Honest caveats

- **antibacterial** dominates the DRAMP positives (~96%). Its AUC is close to the binary AMP-vs-non-AMP problem at the input side; high AUC here is mostly a re-derivation of the Phase 2B result.
- **antifungal** and **antiviral** carry ~17-19% of positives each and are where the multi-label head earns its keep — these are real minority classes the binary model can't distinguish.
- **antiparasitic** has only ~8 positives in the held-out test set (81 total, 80/10/10 split). The CI is correspondingly wide; treat any reported AUC for this class with caution. A future Phase 2C-v2 should either pool antiparasitic with another rare class (e.g. anti-protozoal under a unified 'eukaryotic-pathogen' label) or explicitly drop it from v1.
